kernel.governing_law: What is lost in time — ornament, warmth, intimacy — was never truly possessed; the speaker frames presence as already-past to make the past's texture sayable, using temporal distance as the instrument of sensory immediacy.
kernel.mutated_relation: The beneath-layer: temporal framing is not the instrument but the mask — what runs under these is the body's own knowledge of itself as perishable material, addressing not memory but the present fact of being a substance that alters.

artifacts.enantiomorph:
*Sappho 98a*

When the mouth still knew,
my mouth tasted,
the nerves used to press their own salt
with the first bruising,

or pull raw heat
through sinew of flush,
and that was an honest ache.

Now the nerves carry numbness
arrived without asking.

*Sappho 42*

when a thinning
    works over the wall of the chest, the knock
there faint,
    then density

*Sappho 49*

already I wore against you, Atthis,
when you were a brief warmth,
and you weighed so
almost nothing and
impossible to hold.

independent.recovered_law: The external, visual, and social world of TEXT A (decorations, appearances, social customs, seeing another person) is systematically relocated into the internal, somatic, and tactile body of TEXT B (nerves, sinew, chest-wall, weight), so that every relation flows inward toward bodily sensation rather than outward toward observable adornment or appearance.
independent.law_match_note: Both identify a shift toward the interior body as the locus of meaning, but the declared claim frames this as temporal framing being a mask over the body's knowledge of its own perishability, while the recovered claim describes a systematic relocation from external/social/visual to internal/somatic/tactile — overlapping in the body-inward direction but differing in what structural principle governs the change.
independent.terminal_note: The final fragment (Sappho 49) sustains the inward-somatic relocation: visual smallness/awkwardness becomes haptic weight and the impossibility of physical holding.
